n: Given in September 1830 before six elders in Fayette, this sweeping revelation covers the gathering, the Second Coming, the Millennium, the Creation, and the Fall. Christ introduces himself as the “Great I AM,” whose mercy has atoned for sins.

f.g: the divine name revealed to Moses, identifying Jesus as Jehovah.

n: He will gather his people as a hen gathers her chicks — all who listen, humble themselves, and pray mightily.

f.w: as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings

n: Their sins are forgiven, which is why they can receive this revelation — but they must sin no more to avoid danger.
They are chosen out of the world to preach joyfully, like a trumpet blast.
Be glad: Christ is among them as their advocate with the Father, who is pleased to give them the kingdom.

f.w: it is his good will to give you the kingdom

n: United prayer in faith will be answered.

f.w: Whatsoever ye shall ask in faith

n: They are called to gather the “elect” — those who recognize Christ’s voice and don’t harden their hearts.
The Father has decreed that the elect be gathered to one place on this land to prepare for coming tribulation.
The time is near when the earth is ripe and the proud and wicked will burn like stubble — echoing Malachi.

f.w: all the proud and they that do wickedly shall be as stubble

n: What the apostles prophesied must be fulfilled.
Christ will come in power and glory with heaven’s hosts and reign in righteousness with people on earth for a thousand years — the Millennium.
The original Twelve Apostles will stand at Christ’s right hand at his coming, in a pillar of fire, robed and crowned in glory, to judge the house of Israel.

f.w: to judge the whole house of Israel

n: A trumpet will sound long and loud as at Mount Sinai; the earth will quake, and the righteous dead will rise to be crowned and made one with Christ.

f.w: the dead which died in me

n: Before that day, the sun will darken, the moon turn to blood, and stars fall — signs of the times foretold by prophets.

f.w: the moon shall be turned into blood

n: There will be great mourning among people.
A great hailstorm will destroy crops.
Because the wicked won’t repent, judgment will come. Christ’s blood cannot cleanse those who refuse to hear him.

f.w: the cup of mine indignation is full
my blood shall not cleanse them if they hear me not

n: Plagues of flies and maggots will afflict the wicked — graphic imagery of the consequences of corruption.
Their tongues will be stopped from cursing God, and their bodies will waste away — language closely paralleling Zechariah’s prophecy.

f.w: their flesh shall fall from off their bones, and their eyes from their sockets

n: Beasts and birds will devour their bodies — the great “supper” of Ezekiel and Revelation.

f.w: the fowls of the air shall devour them

n: The “great and abominable church” — all that opposes God — will be destroyed by fire, as Ezekiel foretold.
After the Millennium, people will again deny God, and the earth will be spared only “a little season.”
Then the end will come: heaven and earth will pass away, replaced by a new heaven and new earth.

f.w: a new heaven and a new earth

n: All things will be made new — the earth, people, animals, birds, and fish.
Not one hair or speck will be lost, because all is God’s handiwork. Nothing he made is wasted.

f.g: a tiny particle, like a speck of dust.

n: Before the earth passes away, Michael the archangel (Adam) will sound his trumpet and all the dead will rise.
The righteous will stand at Christ’s right hand to receive eternal life; he will be ashamed to claim the wicked.
To the wicked he will say, “Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire” — Jesus’ words from the parable of the sheep and goats.
He has never said they will return to his presence; they lack the power to go where he is.

f.w: where I am they cannot come

n: Not all of God’s judgments are revealed. His words will be fulfilled — the first shall be last and the last first.
By his Spirit he created all things, both spiritual and temporal.

f.w: by the power of my Spirit created I them

n: Creation was first spiritual, then temporal (physical); the end reverses this — first temporal, then spiritual, as things are glorified.
God speaks this way so we can understand; to him, his works have no beginning or end.
To God all things are spiritual; he has never given a merely temporal law, not even to Adam.

f.w: all things unto me are spiritual

n: God made Adam an agent — free to choose — and gave him spiritual commandments.
Satan existed before Adam. He rebelled, demanding God’s honor and power, and persuaded a third of heaven’s hosts to follow him.

f.w: Give me thine honor, which is my power
a third part of the hosts of heaven

n: They were cast down, becoming the devil and his angels.
A place — hell — was prepared for them from the beginning.
Temptation is necessary for agency: without bitter, we couldn’t know sweet. Opposition makes real choice possible.

f.w: if they never should have bitter they could not know the sweet

n: Satan tempted Adam, who ate the forbidden fruit and became subject to the devil’s influence.
Adam was cast out of Eden and God’s presence, becoming spiritually dead — the “first death,” which is the same as the final spiritual death of the wicked.
God delayed Adam’s physical death until angels could teach him and his descendants repentance and redemption through Christ.

f.w: send forth angels to declare unto them repentance

n: Mortal life is a “probation” — a testing time — so that through physical death believers may rise in immortality to eternal life.
Those who don’t believe face damnation because, without repentance, they cannot be redeemed from their spiritual fall.
They love darkness, and they receive their wages from whomever they choose to obey.

f.w: they receive their wages of whom they list to obey

n: Little children are redeemed from the foundation of the world through Christ.
They cannot sin, because Satan has no power to tempt them until they begin to be accountable.

f.w: until they begin to become accountable

n: God arranged it this way so that great things would be required of parents.

f.w: great things may be required at the hand of their fathers

n: Those with knowledge have been commanded to repent.
Those without understanding remain in God’s merciful hands according to scripture. The revelation ends there.
